Title: A reliable framework for supply chain management using cluster based blockchain for intelligent industrial automation
Text:
A reliable framework for supply 
chain management using cluster 
based blockchain for intelligent 
industrial automation
Eesa Alsolami1, Mahmoud Ahmad Al-khasawenh2,4, Ala Abdulsalam Alarood1, 
Ahmed Omar Alzahrani1, Ahmed Aalameen Ibraheem1 & Mazdak Zamani3
Industrial automation is an integral part of Industry 4.0, and this scenario needs intelligent 
mechanisms to improve the industry’s production level. Manufacturing industries depend entirely on 
supply chain management to track the entire system’s performance, which will be the key term to 
improving product quality. In the modern era of industrial automation, technology entirely depends 
on intelligent computing algorithms. This paper proposes a reliable framework for supply chain 
management using cluster-based blockchain technology. The proposed method contains two main 
contributions. The first is to maintain the information organized using Blockchain Technology, and the 
second is to analyze the Blockchain by extracting valuable information to make an intelligent system 
in industrial automation. The proposed framework’s performance evaluation is based on execution 
time cost analysis for Blockchain, accuracy, and mean error value analysis for the cluster-based project 
key factors classification. Software Development applications with 26 software metrics are used for 
the performance evaluation. The performance analysis for the proposed framework archives 93% for 
software development project clustering concerning the evaluation dataset. The result shows that the 
optimum average size of cluster selection will produce a high accuracy of the suitable Blockchain for 
the new project.
Keywords  Intelligent manufacturing system, Industrial automation, Reliable supply chain management, 
Adversary model, Probability polynomial time algorithm
The supply chain is a management strategy that handles the production or manufacturing of products from raw 
materials to the final product and releases into the market. A well-organized Supply chain management provides 
enough information for the organization to ensure the success in manufacturing the products. Maintaining a 
record of product success rate, loss rate, high-profit area, and raw material cost analysis is mandatory for top and 
middle-level management. The critical parts of SCM are manufacturing and retailing, and its efficiency influences 
other integral parts of the business. Most industrial developments have been transformed into Internet-oriented 
applications. Now, we need intelligent supply chain management, which will provide an efficient way to maintain 
records. One such application area is adopting blockchain technology into supply chain management. Supply 
Chain Management, in general, offers the following services,
Consumer-based service: A well-organized supply chain means the consumer gets the order exactly as 
expected on time. The main expectation from a customer’s point of view is to get accessible support at any point 
in time for every purchase. The Supply Chain Management supports the demand level occasionally to avoid 
overstocking and inventory costs. This method will guide users in managing the supply cost of raw materials, 
transportation, and man management. Speeding up the cash movement into the business will speed up the 
product flow. The clear visibility in Supply Chain Management gives an idea of where to reduce costs and waiting 
times and increase profit margins.

Components of supply chain management
The supply Chain Operations Reference Model is a more effective model, which the Supply Chain Council 
designed to create the best performance for addressing, enhancing, and interacting necessities effectively. This 
reference model has six basic phases: Planning, Sourcing, Location, Product Making, Delivery or Retailing, and 
Returns or Profit Analysis. The following section explains the role of each phase in the Supply Chain Model.
Planning: Provides a detailed view of the operation strategy. Every product manufacturing process has 
benefits and challenges, which should be done strategically.
Sourcing: The next level focuses on procuring raw materials and services acquired from the outsourcing 
companies. This phase involves more cost-oriented analysis based on the best price, on-time delivery, and 
required quantity. Performance analysis is a primary process for assessing the supplier’s quality to achieve 
optimal supply chain management. This is the phase which involves direct cost analysis.
Location: Location is a critical phase in achieving success in supply chain management. Any product 
manufacturing unit must be located to your resource needs and materials.
Making or Manufacturing: In this phase, where assembling, producing, testing and packing activities happen.
Delivery or retailing: Product delivery is based on customer orders and is distributed to different delivery 
points and transport facilities. Product warehousing or inventory management is a key point for making 
intelligent manufacturing.
Returns: This phase involves the feedback or feed-forward mechanism to reduce the defect ratio. This will 
include the process of rework and making changes at the product level or design level. For defective products, 
the company recognized rules for checking performance, cost involvement, and status of detailed records for 
returned products.
Challenges in supply chain management
Industry-based applications were facing several challenges in supply chain management, and some common 
challenges are discussed in this section,
	1.	 Supply chain management becomes a global solution for maintaining a complex supply network; combining 
suppliers, manufacturers, and distributors can be challenging.
	2.	 Accurate demand forecasting is a critical task for efficient supply chain management.
	3.	 Inventory Management is a balancing factor to meet customer requirements by minimizing raw material 
holding costs, and it is a challenging task.
	4.	 Supply chain visibility and lack of real-time scenario visibility in the supply chain lead to inefficiencies and 
difficulties in taking suitable solutions on time.
	5.	 Building and monitoring a strong relationship among suppliers is a critical task. Quality control, financial 
status, and communication gaps can impact the supply chain more.
	6.	 Integrating technological solutions and new technologies (IoT, Blockchain, and AI) with existing supply 
chain systems is another challenging task.
	7.	 Identifying and mitigating risk is a crucial part of supply chain management, and the lack of risk manage­
ment can lead to severe disruption in the supply chain process.
	8.	 Finding skilled professionals is a challenging task in supply chain management.
	9.	 Cyber-attacks are increasing yearly, and protecting sensitive data and ensuring the security of interconnected 
supply chains is a significant challenge.
These challenges can be mitigated with the combination of strategic planning, technological advancements, and 
collaboration with the entire supply chain ecosystem.
Contribution
The following contributions are included in the proposed supply chain management for Industry 4.0 applications.
	a.	 This paper proposed a framework for maintaining supply chain management using the Blockchain Tech­
nique for a fully automated intelligent industry environment. This framework was developed based on the 
Supply Chain Operations Reference Model.
	b.	 This framework design consists of four different stages, which cover the initial planning stage to the sum­
mary of the product’s release into the market. Every small change in the product level will be recorded and 
updated adequately into the Blockchain.
	c.	 Each block in the chain includes critical key points or summary points about the particular block. This will 
enhance the possibility of searching for records from a large number of blocks from a chain in the final block 
or summary block of a proposed Blockchain frame; it is designed with key information about the particular 
product or project.
	d.	 This proposed method uses Cluster-based Blockchain categorization to make information search in an intel­
ligent way for new product designs or project proposals. The Clustering will be done based on the Summary 
Block information. The proposed framework was evaluated by using a software dataset extracted from 17 
open-source projects from GitHub1.

system using a peer-to-peer model known as “Bitcoin” that enables one to carry out online payments without 
the involvement of third-party authority to be present or verified. This is the first identified application of the 
Blockchain Technique. The distributed ledger mechanism is followed to replace the traditional database in

Methods
This section discussed the general framework for the supply chain management technique and the basic 
assumption for the proposed framework. This section discussed the generalized supply chain management 
technique for product manufacturing methods. Any industry could adopt this architecture for product 
development. This architecture is designed for product manufacturing based on the Supply Chain Operations 
Reference Model.
According to Supply chain management, a central controlling node or a system is mandatory for monitoring 
the activities of the product development life cycle. The architecture consists of various phases, such as financial 
service, raw material department, inventory maintenance, service partners, manufacturing unit, testing 
professionals, transport and delivery, retail, and feedback system. The following section explains the roles and 
responsibilities of each phase in general Blockchain, as given in Fig. 1.
Any product manufacturing system fully depends on the part of the financial services department. This phase 
has to give clearance for the planning and design of any product development. The raw material department is 
directly connected with the production department. The product outcome depends on the timely supply of raw 
materials. Product quality is directly linked to the quality of raw materials. The raw material department is fully 
controlled by direct cost involvement, and most of the supply chain management is occupied by raw materials. 
The raw material and inventory maintenance has to be given equal weight to the supply chain management. 
The raw materials are purchased purely based on the availability status maintained by the inventory details. In 
supply chain management, inventory maintenance plays a significant role in purchasing materials for the service 
or material providers. They are third-party service providers for the smooth running of product manufacturing, 
and they are doing some parallel activities to reduce product delivery time for customers. They are involved 
with the product manufacturing unit with direct cost involvement. The manufacturing unit is responsible for 
product development based on the customer needs. This phase is a combination of employees, management, 
and customers for product development. This is a combination of the Internal Auditing team and the External 
Testing team. The role of internal audit is an important checkpoint for enhancing the excellence of the product, 
and this will reduce the maximum number of errors during the development stage itself. The third part of the 
audit is product-level testing to identify the defects. Testing is a systematic approach to improving the quality of a 
product, and this is an important task for supply chain management. The products are delivered to the customers 
based on their orders through an effective transport mode. The cost involved in this phase is an indirect cost, and 
this will be reflected in the retail price of the product in the market. The role of retail shops is an important node

A smart contract plays an important role in the proposed technique, and this will establish a reliable framework 
for supply chain management within a cluster-based blockchain for intelligent industrial automation. Smart 
contracts are self-executable programs stored on a Blockchain that autonomously enforce agreements between 
industrial agencies without using intermediaries. The proposed supply chain technique will facilitate transparent, 
immutable, and automated transactions, ensuring trust and efficiency among stakeholders. The cluster-based 
Blockchain will ensure enhanced data consistency and security by validating and executing redefined conditions 
across multiple layers to prevent fraud and manipulation. These contracts streamline critical operations, like 
requirement analysis, internal auditing, payments, coding development, and compliance verification, and this 
will reduce intermedia interventions and errors.
Case study: software development life cycle model
The proposed reliable framework for supply chain management using the Blockchain technique is tested with a 
software product manufacturing unit. Most product manufacturing companies use supply chain management to 
improve the quality and productivity of products. These methods take various factors into account to improve 
the efficiency of product manufacturing. According to the survey on the application of supply chain management 
in software development, the life cycle is still open, and this area needs more attention. This paper is taking the 
initiative to design a supply chain management framework for the software development life cycle. The following 
section provides an overview of the Software Development Life Cycle. The supply chain management for the 
software development is given as a framework, and the blocks are developed based on the outcome of each phase.

Overview of SDLC model
Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) is a systematic approach used in software industries to design, 
implement, and test high-quality software. The SDLC’s purpose is to generate high-quality software that meets 
or satisfies customers’ expectations and reaches a conclusion within the given time limits and cost estimation. 
SDLC is a framework that consists of various phases in the development of software. ISO/IEC 12,207 is a 
global standard for software development lifecycle. It proposes to be the benchmark that describes all the tasks 
mandatory for the implementation and maintaining software.
SDLC is a team work done by the software development team members, including external service providers. 
It contains complete planning about how to design, maintain, exchange, modify or improve specific software.
Figure 2 provides a graphical illustration of the several stages elaborate in a typical SDLC. A more general 
SDLC consists of six stages, and the following section explains SDLC stages,
Planning and requirement analysis
In the Requirement investigation phase, senior members of a team collect inputs from the customers, sales 
department, survey from market analysis and domain expert suggestions for the most appropriate software 
product for the consumers. This phase is the most significant and essential stage in SDLC. This data is used to 
plan the project methods and conduct a product likelihood study in the economic, working, and practical areas.
Planning is critical for the quality guarantee requirements, and identifying the risks associated with the 
project is also prepared in this stage. The conclusion received from the technical feasibility study is to describe 
the several technical methods that can be followed to develop the project with minimum risks.
Defining requirements
Next to the requirement analysis is defining and documenting the product requirements. This will be created 
using the SRS (Software Requirement Specification) document, which comprises all the product requirements 
to be developed during the project life cycle.
Designing the product architecture
SRS is the point of reference for product design to come up with a suitable architecture for developing software 
products. Based on the SRS, usually, more than one design method for the product design is planned and 
recorded in a DDS - Design Document Specification. This will be presented to all the shareholders, and based 
on several constraints such as assessment of risk, robustness of product, modularity in design, budget planning, 
and time constraints, the suitable design method is chosen for the particular product.
Implementation or developing the product
This stage in SDLC generates programming code as per DDS. If the design is achieved in a comprehensive way and 
well-organized manner, code generation can be skilful without much difficulty. Designers must follow guidelines 
given for the coding well-defined by their companies, and tools used in programming, like interpreters, editors, 
compilers, debuggers, etc., are used to produce the code. Different sets of high-level languages, such as C, C++, 
Pascal, Java and PHP, are used to produce codes.
Testing the product
This stage will be a subsection of all other stages in standard SDLC models. This stage is denoted as the testing-
only stage of the software product, where product errors or defects are described, followed, fixed and retested 
until the product attains the quality and standards given in the SRS.
Deployment in the market and maintenance
Once the testing stage is completed and the software product is prepared to be implemented, it is formally 
reached in the suitable marketplace. Sometimes, software product implementation happens in phases based on 
the business needs of that company. The software may be reached in a limited sector and tested in the real-time 
business environment.

Experimentation, results and discussion
This section consists of two subdivisions: the runtime cost analysis for the proposed Blockchain frame with 
ClariNet Tool and the performance evaluation for the proposed cluster techniques for grouping the Blockchain. 
The evaluation is done based on the software development life cycle model for software industry projects.
Runtime cost analysis for blockchain framework
Every change on the block from the chain required some cost in terms of execution costs and transaction costs. 
The execution costs are divided into five different categories: Run time, Read counts, Read Length in Bytes, Write 
counts, and Write Length in Bytes. The Run time costs are calculated based on the overall complexity of the code 
that can be executed to create a blockchain. Read count means how many times the memory or chain state is 
accessed to extract information. This will count the constants, variables, and intermediate variables created for 
the particular block in a chain. The read length, in bytes, means how much data we can read from the memory 
of the chain. The Write count and Write length mean how many times the write operation is performed over the 
chain and how much data we can write to the chain.
The operation based on read and write is limited, and it is practically static. The run time cost analysis is 
more dynamic. As a Blockchain developer, they have to be careful with how they structure their code and which 
functions they use. These functions may be called a few times per block to create or update the blocks. Cost 
analysis is a challenging task, and it is performed using the Clarinet Tool. This tool has cost analysis features as 
a built-in function, and it has two varieties of analysis: manual analysis and automated analysis. In the manual 
analysis, the developer enters the inputs manually. In the automated analysis, the developer will give an automatic 
test function. The proposed Blockchain framework was evaluated through automatic runtime cost analysis by 
using a stranded set of reading, writing, and hashing operations. Table 1 below provides runtime cost analysis 
for every update in the block.
The block size is 1558 Bytes, and SHA-128 is the cryptographic hash function used to calculate the hash 
value. The hash value will be computed for each block in the chain. The digital signature has been computed and 
generated by using public key algorithms, and the block encryption can be done by using a symmetric encryption 
algorithm. The number of hash functions, digital signs, and encryption usage depends on the number of blocks 
in a chain. The average runtime cost for hash code generation for SHA 128 is 128 µ s, and the average run time 
cost for digital signature and symmetric encryption is 195 µ s and 156 µ s, respectively.

Conclusion and future scope data availability
This paper proposed a reliable framework for supply chain management (SCM) by integrating cluster-based 
Blockchain with intelligent industrial automation. This technique will enhance the transparency, security, and 
efficiency by addressing security pitfalls present in the supply chain management. This technique will improve the 
data integrity, real-time monitoring, and trust among stakeholders involved in the industrial automation. This 
cluster-based Blockchain mechanism optimizes transaction processing and reduces computational overhead by 
maintaining decentralization with security enhancements. Intelligent automation ensures continuous operations 
by using smart contracts by maintaining a summary block for each transaction, and this improvement will 
enhance and streamline decision-making processes. Experimental results show that the proposed technique 
achieves efficiency for updating future transactions instantaneously, and it shows that the proposed framework 
is improving traceability, reducing delays, and mitigating fraud risks in supply chain networks.
The performance evaluation for the proposed framework is done based on execution time cost analysis for 
Blockchain and accuracy and mean error value analysis for the cluster-based project key factors classification. 
Software development applications with 26 software metrics were used for the performance evaluation. The 
dataset contains 703 anonymized entries with four different sets of software metrics, which are used to train the 
proposed framework. This method could produce only 72% for cluster size 5. The performance analysis for the 
proposed framework archives 93% for project clustering with respect to the evaluation dataset. The accuracy
